items.stem: What is the finding of the AAA survey?

choices.text: The majority of drivers prefer to drive and park themselves.
choices.zh: 大多数驾驶员更喜欢自己驾驶和停车。

choices.text: Human drivers become easily distracted or tired while driving.
choices.zh: 人类驾驶员在驾驶时容易分心或疲劳。

choices.text: Most drivers feel uncertain about the safety of self-driving cars.
choices.zh: 大多数驾驶员对自动驾驶汽车的安全性感到不确定。

choices.text: Most drivers have test driven cars with automatic braking features.
choices.zh: 大多数驾驶员已经试驾过具有自动刹车功能的汽车。

items.stem: What does John Nielsen say about self-driving cars?

choices.text: Their drivers would feel safe after getting used to the automatic devices.
choices.zh: 驾驶员在习惯自动装置后会感到安全。

choices.text: They would be unpopular with drivers who only trust their own skills.
choices.zh: 它们不会受到那些只相信自己技能的驾驶员的欢迎。

choices.text: Their increased comfort levels have boosted their sales.
choices.zh: 它们舒适度的提升促进了销量的增长。

choices.text: They are not actually as safe as automakers advertise.
choices.zh: 它们实际上并不像汽车制造商宣传的那样安全。

items.stem: What do we learn from the talk about wild carrots?

choices.text: They have small roots.
They grow white flowers.
They taste like apples.
They come from Central Africa.

items.stem: What does the speaker say about carrots in the late 1500s?

choices.text: They turned from white to purple in color.
choices.zh: 它们的颜色从白色变成了紫色。

choices.text: They became popular on the world market.
choices.zh: 它们在世界市场上变得流行起来。

choices.text: They became an important food for humans.
choices.zh: 它们成为人类的重要食物。

choices.text: They began to look like modern-day carrots.
choices.zh: 它们开始看起来像现代的胡萝卜。

items.stem: Why did people turn to carrots for food during the two world wars?

choices.text: They were found quite nutritious.
choices.zh: 人们发现它们营养丰富。

choices.text: There were serious food shortages.
choices.zh: 出现了严重的粮食短缺。

choices.text: People discovered their medicinal value.
choices.zh: 人们发现了它们的药用价值。

choices.text: Farm machines helped lower their prices.
choices.zh: 农业机械帮助降低了它们的价格。

items.stem: What was one particular convenience Katherine loved about Facebook?

choices.text: She could update her family any time she liked.
choices.zh: 她可以在任何时候更新家人的动态。

choices.text: She could call up her family whenever she liked
choices.zh: 她可以在任何时候给家人打电话。

choices.text: She could locate her friends wherever they were.
choices.zh: 她可以定位朋友们无论他们在哪里。

choices.text: She could download as many pictures as she liked.
choices.zh: 她可以下载任意多的图片。

items.stem: How did Katherine feel when her classmates added her as a Facebook friend?

choices.text: She liked to inform her friends about her success.
choices.zh: 她喜欢告诉朋友们她的成功。

choices.text: She enjoyed reading her friends' status updates.
choices.zh: 她喜欢阅读朋友们的状态更新。

choices.text: She felt quite popular among them.
choices.zh: 她觉得自己在他们当中很受欢迎。

choices.text: She felt she was a teenager again.
choices.zh: 她感觉自己又变回了少女。

items.stem: What made Katherine feel bad about herself later on?

choices.text: She could barely respond to all her 500 Facebook friends.
choices.zh: 她几乎无法回应她所有500个Facebook好友。

choices.text: She spent more time updating her friends than her family.
choices.zh: 她花在更新朋友动态上的时间比陪伴家人的时间还多。

choices.text: She could barely balance Facebook updates and her work.
choices.zh: 她几乎无法平衡Facebook更新和工作。

choices.text: She didn't seem to be doing as well as her Facebook friends.
choices.zh: 她似乎过得不如她的Facebook好友们好。

choices.text: They can work longer than donkeys.

choices.text: It was brought over from Spain.

choices.zh: 它是由一位美国大使捐赠的。

choices.text: They participated in a mule-driving competition.

choices.text: They fed mules with the best food they could find.
choices.zh: 他们用能找到的最好的食物喂骡子。
